| #978 | The sink's lane exemption has three measured shapes it still destroys silently | open | bundle-976-977-978 | Measured by the adversarial review of the #973 sink guard during the bundle-973-974-975 run. All three are destroyed equally by the pre-change code, so these are residuals rather than regressions — filed because the guard is otherwise easy to read as absolute, and the CHANGELOG now says so in prose that a later reader may reasonably want closed. That bundle taught Step 0's clean-worktree guard to see untracked work: the probe widened from --untracked-files=no to -uall, and worktreeDirtRecords keeps every tracked record while filtering ?? records through isParkedLanePath(rel, []). The guard is sound in both directions — verified against the real sink CLI, refusing over a genuine file and over a self-referential symlink, while an ordinary lane-only run still completes and an over-broadening mutation refuses that ordinary run. These three shapes escape the classifier rather than the probe. (1) A filename containing backslashes — backslashes are legal in POSIX filenames, and isParkedLanePath normalises \ to / before testing, so a plain file literally named kaola-workflow\proj\x.md decodes correctly and then classifies as lane, exempted and destroyed. (2) An embedded git repository under a lane prefix — a nested worktree at, say, .kw/worktrees/nested/ is reported as one collapsed record even under -uall because git does not descend into another repository, the single record is exempted by its directory segment, and everything uncommitted inside it goes with the removal; this is the exception to the "one record per file" rationale that -uall was chosen for. (3) The legacy route removes the run's own .cache/ journal — the --sink route stages a best-effort rescue of <wt>/kaola-workflow/<project>/ before removal (sink-merge.js:2100-2130) so untracked .cache evidence survives there, but the legacy route has no equivalent and its rescue is try/catch best-effort covering only the own project. For whoever takes it: the fix must not break the two things the guard is balanced against — widening the exemption test breaks arm (f), since every ordinary run leaves untracked lane content and a bare widening refuses every sink, and reaching past --untracked-files into --ignored breaks arm (g), where nothing else in the 942-assertion suite catches that mutation; both arms are already in scripts/test-sink-merge.js. SPECIFY THE RESULT: the sink does not silently destroy uncommitted work in any of these three shapes — whether that is a stricter lane predicate, a descent into collapsed records, a rescue on the legacy route, or something else, is open. |

The shim was audited against real GNU coreutils 9.1 in a container and matched all 13 load-bearing rows including modes and the exact "too few X's in template" abort; two divergences were recorded, both STRICTER than real GNU: mid-template X handling and -p/-t precedence. | #983 | The sink stage's unreadable-file trigger is unfixtured, because EACCES fixtures invert under root | open | TBD | A deliberate, named test gap from bundle-976-977-978, filed so it stays visible rather than living only in a code comment. The #978 review found a stage copy that THROWS was swallowed, letting the sink destroy the run's journal at exit 0 while reporting success; that is now closed on BOTH routes, pinned by arms (m) and (n) in test-sink-merge.js across all four editions and mutation-partitioned (disabling the legacy repair reds exactly (m), disabling the --sink repair reds exactly (n)). Both arms drive SYMLINK triggers only — dangling and self-referential in one fixture, since whichever the copy meets first loses the whole stage, so one arm covers both without depending on readdir order. The unreadable-file (EACCES) trigger was deliberately NOT fixtured because a permission fixture INVERTS UNDER ROOT (chmod 000 does not deny root), so the pin would silently pass for the wrong reason — a fixture that cannot fail is worse than a documented gap. NOT CLAIMED: that EACCES is broken; mechanically it would likely take the same refuse-on-throw path since the repair keys on the throw rather than its cause, but it was never driven, so the honest statement is "not covered", not "does not work". SPECIFY THE RESULT: either an oracle that observes the trigger and cannot pass for the wrong reason under root, or a recorded demonstration that it reaches the same refusal so no separate oracle is owed. |

## Rules

- A separate roadmap/research session owns discovering and adding future work to GitHub issues.
- `workflow-next` fetches GitHub issues and mirrors active implementation work here.
- After each `workflow-next` cycle, refresh this file from issue state.
- Move completed workflow project folders to `kaola-workflow/archive/`.
- Close linked GitHub issues only after acceptance criteria pass.
- Keep commit and push as the final Finalization step after docs, issues, roadmap, archive, and metadata are complete.

### Project rules
## The design — read `docs/decisions/0017-the-mission-list.md` first

**The derivation is finished and the owner has ruled.** The work is now **build ADR 0017**.
ADR 0016 is its predecessor and still worth reading, but where the two disagree, 0017 wins.

### The premise

The workflow was built when agents were weak orchestrators, so it encoded orchestration **as
constraint**. That premise expired, and 0017 acts on the consequence 0016 stopped short of: if the
agent orchestrates itself, the plan need not be a machine-readable schedule.

**The existence proof is observed, not argued.** A bare session — no framework, no plan, no gates, no
bookkeeping, given only the main-orchestrator role plus a goal — decomposed the work, ran six
concurrent subagents across disjoint files with no conflicts, found real defects, and did not drift.

### What the design is

**One file per run. Four fields per item — `item` / `status` / `dispatched` / `result` — written at
three moments** (created, dispatched, closed), plus a header line carrying the goal. No script is
required; a file convention suffices. An item is a mission in one line of prose: hints and facts,
never a prescription. Tools are what the orchestrator already reaches for — subagents, worktrees —
offered and declinable.

### The governing rule for every change

> **Derive ADDITIVELY. Add only what an observed failure demands. Silence is an answer.**

Subtractive derivation asks *"may I remove this?"*, and there is always an answer that keeps it —
three separate passes of the 0017 discussion preserved machinery under *"harder to reason about"*
dressed as *"permits irreversible harm"*. Additive derivation asks *"what forced this to exist?"*

0016's **delete the verdict, keep the measurement** still governs anything that survives.

### Nothing refuses

The refusal count is **zero**. R1 was never armable, the consent valve is the orchestrator asking the
user, and R3 is now a report.

**Concurrency carries no machinery at all** — no antichain sweep, no disjointness check, no
serializer taxonomy, no evidence line, no caps. Disjointness is the agent's call, with no inspection.

### Owner rulings — do not re-litigate

- **The sink reports; the orchestrator owns the outcome.** *Supersedes the 2026-07-29 "R3 survives
  permanently" ruling.* The sink says what it found; the orchestrator gets the branch right — correct
  merge, resynchronize, or **file a PR** — and cleans up after. The change is not refuse-versus-proceed;
  it is **who is accountable for the branch ending up right.**
- **Any form of regulation or structure is limiting.** A mechanism justified by *"the agent might get
  this wrong"* argues against the design's premise rather than for a gate.
- **Do not over-complicate. There is already too much in this project.**
- **No run-cost ledger is built.** *(Stands from 2026-07-29.)* Residual risk accepted: if it recurs,
  it recurs silently.

### Watch-list discipline

Mechanisms derived for failure classes **never observed** in this methodology are recorded, not
built — see `docs/decisions/0017-the-mission-list.md` § *The watch list*. Each row names the
observation that would arm it, and a row whose mechanism was built and later removed names the commit
to recover it from. **Do not build one speculatively.**

### Working rules that survive

- **The unit of progress is a MECHANISM removed. Never a test removed.** Tests fall out with the
  mechanism.
- **A tool the agent is forced to use is a gate wearing a tool's name.** Test: can the agent decline
  it and still finish?
- **Correctness is never traded for the count.** A defect found while cutting gets fixed even when
  the fix adds code.
- **Premises get measured before they get built on.** A premise that collapses is the result, not a
  setback — and this cuts both ways. Two capability claims in the corpus turned out to be untraced:
  #854 row 9's *"every traced run silently serialized"* is a **tooling** defect (`open-next`
  single-opened a frontier the planner had authored as parallel), and 0016's *"a missing reviewer
  produces a merge"* cites no trace at all.
- **Grade against driven behaviour, never the condition census.** It is a sound ratchet and an index
  of emission sites. It is not a population.
- **Convergence is weaker evidence than it looks. Prefer the disagreements.**
